data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's proposed distinguishing evidence—errors clustering on multi-feature integration tasks—does not distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere compliance because it is a property of the checklist's design, not of the panel's judgment process. Whether the panel fails on integration tasks depends entirely on whether the checklist encodes conditional logic, which SRC_002 itself concedes in its counterconditions. If the checklist does encode interactions, the panel will succeed on integration tasks via pure compliance; if it does not, the panel will fail via pure compliance. In neither case does the error-clustering pattern reveal anything about whether the panel is exercising genuine judgment versus mechanically following the checklist, which is precisely what the problem asks to distinguish.
